item.title: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
item.description: While that was the first official Peanuts comic, a similar version by Charles Schulz predated Peanuts and ran in Minnesota’s St. Paul Pioneer Press. It was called Li’l Folks and also starred cute little children, although it did not have a regular cast like Peanuts would. Li’l Folks ran from 1947 until 1950, when Schulz quit after his editor refused to give him a raise from the $10 per comic he was making. After that, Schulz brought Li’l Folks to United Feature Syndicate. The national cartoon syndicator liked the comic, but needed to change its name because of a 1930s comic strip called Little Folks . The name Peanuts was chosen because The Howdy Doody Show was popular at the time and the studio audience of children on the show was called the “Peanut gallery.” Thus, Peanuts became the name.

item.title: 5 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics About Food Only Charles Schulz Could Come Up With
item.description: There aren't quite as many Peanuts comic strips focused on food as one might expect. Little kids do tend to live their lives in the windows between meals and snacks, and Snoopy is as obsessed with his suppertime as any other dog, but food humor was a relatively low priority in Charles Schulz's punchline rotation. Compared to baseball, philosophy, Snoopy's alternate personas, or Charlie Brown's truly existential levels of depression , food as a topic in Peanuts was kept on a low boil.

item.title: 8 Near-Perfect Xbox 360 Games That Are Forgotten Masterpieces
item.description: The Xbox 360 era was a marvelous generation and the last time publishers regularly bet on strange, original ideas. Plenty of those bets paid off, from Gears of War to Assassin's Creed . But time hasn't been kind to all of them, and some of the generation's best games have been out of the conversation so long that a whole new wave of players has never heard of them.

item.title: 44 Years Later, Star Trek’s Best Quote About Grief Is Still a Near-Perfect Sci-Fi Moment
item.description: Franchises often help us understand the pain of loss. Shows like WandaVision have been praised for their exploration of grief and the anguish that exists there. But other franchises have also explored the feelings that surround death and grief. One of the biggest science fiction franchises of all time is known for quite a few poignant moments exploring what death can bring to those who are left behind. That franchise is Star Trek and trying to figure out the best approach to loss is hard because each of the franchise's iconic series has had moments that are worth talking about.

item.title: Steam Makes Popular World War II Strategy Game Free to Play This Weekend
item.description: Steam regularly gives PC players an opportunity to try something new without spending a cent and these promotions are particularly useful for strategy fans , as they offer a chance to test out a new experience before deciding whether it's worth the investment.

item.title: Sony's Bringing Back Spider-Man $2.5 Billion Hit With New Footage
item.description: As Marvel Studios' release of Avengers Endgame: Encore proves, blockbuster movies can still dominate the box office , even after a multibillion dollar run. Sony is planning a rerelease of Spider-Man: Brand New Day to bring web-head-heads back to movie theaters — and like Endgame: Encore , the studio is adding new footage of Spider-Man 's latest flick as an incentive.

item.title: 'Avatar: Seven Havens’ Season 2 Release Date Announcement Includes Some Shocking Good News
item.description: Avatar: Seven Havens spent its entire first season in the Haven of Ellora, but as the show's title makes clear, that's just one of many Havens spread across this post-apocalyptic landscape. Paramount Plus announced Thursday that Book 2: Discovery premieres surprisingly soon, while also confirming that Avatar Pavi’s (Saheli Khan) journey to repair the broken world is about to pick up speed. The announcement, which also confirms Avatar: Seven Havens Book 3 will come soon after Book 2, includes a synopsis that answers some of our most pressing questions following the season 1 finale: Is this now Pavi’s story? What will happen to Nisha (Aishu Devan)? Where will the plot take them and when will they reunite? Already, we’re getting answers to these and other questions.

item.title: Daniel Craig's Most Disappointing Bond Film Quietly Exits Streaming This Month
item.description: Daniel Craig's time as James Bond may be over, but his legacy as the iconic British spy is still being felt across Hollywood. After five films and 15 years in the role, Craig helped usher in a grittier era for the long-running franchise, delivering some of 007's most memorable big-screen adventures along the way.

item.title: Ghost Rider Star Says He's Down to Return for Marvel's 2028 Reboot
item.description: Marvel Studios is bringing back the supernatural hero Ghost Rider in a new movie in 2028, with Ryan Gosling in the lead role . Exactly which version of Ghost Rider Gosling will tackle remains unclear, but one former actor who donned the flaming skull says he's down to ride alongside the rebooted silver screen Spirit of Vengeance if Marvel calls: Agents of SHIELD star Gabriel Luna.
